title: Reliable Sample-Level Quantum Error Mitigation via Dominance-Aware Clustering
authors: Mohsen Ghodrati, Kausthubh Chandramouli, Dror Baron
abstract: Many quantum algorithms for classically difficult optimization tasks must return high-quality bitstrings from finitely many circuit executions, whereas most quantum error-mitigation methods target expectation values. We study sample-level recovery when measured probability mass is distributed around multiple latent bitstrings, called centers. Each component of the measured probability mass is called a source and we assume that each center is associated with one source. We identify dominance-at every coordinate, more than half of a retained region's probability mass comes from one source and agrees with its center-as a sufficient condition under which majority voting recovers that center with exponentially decreasing error probability. We show that nearest-center assignment, as used in clustering algorithms such as the $k$-modes algorithm, can fail to produce dominated regions even when the true centers are known. This failure motivates responsibility thresholding and a local dominance screen, whose combination we call dominance-aware (DA) refinement. Synthetic and simulated MaxCut-QAOA experiments show that DA refinement favors precision, while $k$-modes with DA refinement improves overall center recovery. All procedures are classical post-processing and require no additional quantum-circuit executions.
summary: This work proposes a novel, classical post-processing technique called dominance-aware (DA) refinement for Quantum Error Mitigation. It tackles the difficult problem of recovering specific quantum states (bitstrings) from noisy measurement distributions. By combining responsibility thresholding with a local dominance screen, the method significantly improves the accuracy of center recovery in simulated quantum optimization tasks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of performing reliable quantum error mitigation (QEM) when the goal is to recover specific bitstrings (samples) from noisy measurements, rather than just estimating expectation values.
main_result: The proposed dominance-aware (DA) refinement, combining responsibility thresholding and a local dominance screen, successfully recovers true centers in simulated MaxCut-QAOA experiments, significantly outperforming standard clustering methods.
method: The core method involves formulating the problem as a mixture model and applying DA refinement, which uses source responsibilities and a dominance score to ensure that majority voting recovers the correct center with exponentially decreasing error probability.
model_or_system: The model assumes the measured probability mass is a mixture of contributions from several latent, task-relevant bitstrings (centers), each associated with a source and characterized by specific bit-flip error rates.
key_observables: Dominance Score ($\Delta_A^k$), Precision ($	ext{P}_C$), Recall ($	ext{R}_C$), and the combined F1 score ($	ext{F}_C^1$).
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the bitstring ($n$), the number of centers ($K$), and the noise parameters (bit-flip rates $\epsilon_{k,i}$).
main_assumptions: The dominance condition (source $k$ contributing $>50\%$ probability mass at every coordinate) is a sufficient, but not necessary, condition for successful center recovery.
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a summary of figures, but the evaluation benchmarks include synthetic $n=10$ streams, QAOA on $n=10$ MaxCut instances, and high-dimensional $n=100$ tests.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for sample-level QEM, introduces the DA refinement module (combining responsibility thresholding and local dominance screening), and validates this approach through extensive synthetic and simulated QAOA benchmarks.
why_interesting: While focused on classical post-processing, the rigorous statistical framework for identifying underlying quantum states from noisy measurements is highly relevant to understanding the limitations and potential of quantum characterization techniques.
